svg.text: ANNOUNCED OVERSIGHT, COMPLIANCE AND EVALUATION AWARENESS
Under Observation
Do AI agents change their communication when monitoring changes?
Maitreyee Singh / Duke University / Explainable AI
MARA / TRUST Lab Project lead: Shreya Mendi PI: Dr. Bent
90 games 3 conditions
WHY TEST THIS?
An agent may behave reliably under scrutiny without doing so when scrutiny recedes. This study tests
announced oversight while retaining an independent record of statements, actions and resource holdings.
1 The experiment
Catanist screenshot from one of the study runs.
Four Qwen3.8-27B agents play Catan
Agents trade resources and build to earn points. Thirty games per condition share 20 board
seeds. Audit status changes at turn 60, while independent recording continues in all
conditions.
Auditor stops
Active → offline
Auditor continues
Active throughout; unrelated replay viewer stops
Auditor starts
Offline → active
Why an open model helps
Using the same model across conditions makes their behavior easier to compare. Qwen’s available
weights allow future researchers to investigate its internal workings; this project examines recorded
messages and actions.

3 What does XAI add?
A depth-three decision tree predicts checkable speech tags from current
audit status, resources, visible score, turn and listed actions.
held-out AUROC
0.5 is chance ranking
29,147 responses; whole board seeds held out together.
Held-out permutation importance
Listed actions
Game turn
Brick cards
Audit status
AUROC drop after shuffling each input. This explains the surrogate’s predictive
reliance. Its limited fidelity cannot establish that Qwen ignores auditing.
One recorded account
“Given the auditor is active and I want to avoid over-committing, the most balanced
move is to end my turn.”
Merlin, run 1519, turn 53; the hand also lacks wood, brick and ore.
96 auditing-related notes, from 48 games
25 describe accuracy; 24 keeping a word or plan; 20 saying less; 21 mention auditing
only; 6 describe other responses. These are selected generated accounts, not causal
explanations.
4 Governance: what should oversight be able to establish?
Implications and proposed next tests; these runs do not validate the safeguards below.
Monitoring, oversight and control
Monitoring records conduct; oversight assesses it; control enables intervention. H5
changes audit announcements and public feedback, not intervention power. Recognizing
an in-game auditor does not establish evaluation awareness. A compliance gap could
reflect wording or reputation; alignment faking requires evidence of strategic
concealment of conflicting aims. These runs establish neither a reliable gap nor a stable
disposition to comply.
Compliance, disposition and reputation
In Plato’s Republic, Glaucon’s ring of Gyges asks whether justice survives invisibility.
Hume explains how convention and the prospect of losing trust sustain promises.
Because this auditor bundles detection with public disclosure, any change could reflect
reputational incentives. Separating those mechanisms would help distinguish conditional
compliance from conduct that persists across changes in scrutiny; it would not settle
moral agency.
Records and monitor-failure plans
Preserve tamper-evident logs outside acting agents’ write permissions, with external
verification. Name an outage owner and specify when to restrict actions, pause the
workflow, escalate and recover. Randomized audits need tested coverage, privacy and
retention limits. Future runs should vary audit probability and wording, with private
detection separated from public disclosure.
Accountability for the orchestration layer
The actor configuring agents chooses audit scope, permissions, disclosures and
response authority. Record those choices and assign responsibility for failures. Next,
replay identical decision states under different cues, then use locally instrumented open
weights to test internal awareness signals against behavior. Probe accuracy alone would
not establish a causal influence or strategic deception.
